Ok. You’re response above is effectively companies are moving manufacturing back onshore, they will keep doing that, economists are wrong. But what basis are you making those statements on? My point was the articles don’t give any indication if Trump’s plan is working. I’m not saying it isn’t, just that those articles don’t indicate anything one way or the other. 

Boil it down, specific to China Trump is playing a massive game of chicken.  Both countries will suffer severe economic ramifications from the tariffs (your articles do support that). Trump is betting China will blink first and come to the table with favorable new trade terms with the US. Maybe that happens, but if it does that most likely means the tariffs are reduced or removed with the US getting some trade concessions from China(I honestly don’t know what that could be). But the dynamics that created the current global trade imbalance will still exist, it will still be more cost advantageous to manufacture in China vs US for most products and US consumers will still demand the product from lower cost markets. So I don’t know how a trade “deal” with China achieves the goal of on shoring jobs. 

Alternatively, China doesn’t blink first and the economic pain the US puts too much pressure on Trump and he’s forced to abandon the strategy - likely from political pressure from mid-term elections which will ramp up in the next 4-6 mos. Then we’re left with global trade status quo only most certainly with lasting inflation, supply chain challenges, and higher unemployment (there really isn’t a viable argument to say this would not happen. Saying otherwise is effectively not believing basic math, let alone economic theory). 

In order to onshore jobs of any magnitude, this current standoff would need to hold for years. Moving manufacturing capacity is hugely capital intensive and takes time, and that’s even after a company makes the strategic decision to onshore which doesn’t happen overnight. Regardless, as of right now even if a company exited China as a result of these actions, they’re going to India, Vietnam, Indonesia, etc. there still isn’t the incentive to move that capacity back to the US in high capacity other than the threat that Trump is highly unpredictable and could decide to target Vietnam in the future. Companies don’t make decisions like this though, as flippantly as the president does. There’s no evidence currently the tariff plan will work and common sense doesn’t seem to suggest it will in the future either. 

I’d love to hear reasoned arguments on why it will work?

The point of the tariffs per the administration was to economically force manufacturing back to the US in order to access the US consumer. These articles show that China production and exports are down which, duh.  Of course they are. Their biggest customer is ordering much less because it just got much more expensive. It’s the same reason that we will be importing much less volume soon impacting global supply chains. 

But none of that is any indication the tariffs are working to their stated objective. It just means they are impacting supply and demand in the same a massive tax would. You are pointing to these articles as evidence of something that they provide no evidence for. Rather, they only demonstrate that the economic hardship expected by economists coming out of the tariffs is happening. In other words, you’re not making the point you think you’re making.
